Data Cleaning and Preparation The cleaned data-set ends up with 612 rows and 9 variables , and saved as rental_data_final_epfl_612.csv for further analysis.

Explanation parse_number(): I used it to clean numeric strings that contain suffixes or symbols. To prevent extreme distortions caused by outliers in price_m2 often produced by incorrectly recorded very small surface values, we filter out infinite values, NAs, and keep only logically coherent ranges of living area. parse_number() It’s use to find the first numbers inside of a chain of text, ignoring characters or other symbols, spaces or commas

Analysis

Part 5.

COMMENTS

Price Comparison: The violin and box plots indicate that “On request” properties tend to have higher overall price levels and a broader upper tail distribution, suggesting more expensive and high end listings compared to available properties. Living Space Comparison: “On Request properties also tend to have larger living areas, suggesting that listings with hidden prices are typically bigger homes or apartments. Floor Comparison: The floor distribution shows that both “Available” and “On Request” properties appear across similar floor levels, with no clear bias toward any specific floors in either group.

Part 6. Statistical Summary and Hypothesis Testing for Price for Square Meter

Statistical Summary of Price per m² by Property Status
is_hidden count median mean sd min max
Available 373 33.20000 34.41561 10.972466 8.301887 129.75000
On Request 132 33.06718 33.93496 9.278312 17.500000 71.42857

COMMENTS: ” On Request” properties show higher average and median price per square meter, along with a wider spread in values. The larger standard deviation, minimum, and maximum suggest greater variability and the presence of more high end listings in this group.

Part 6.1 T-Test

## 
##  Welch Two Sample t-test
## 
## data:  price_m2 by is_hidden
## t = 0.48678, df = 269.51, p-value = 0.6268
## alternative hypothesis: true difference in means between group Available and group On Request is not equal to 0
## 95 percent confidence interval:
##  -1.463340  2.424638
## sample estimates:
##  mean in group Available mean in group On Request 
##                 34.41561                 33.93496

CONCLUSION: The t‑test shows no statistically significant differece in average price per square meter between “Available” and “On Request” properties. The small numerical gap seen in the descriptive summary is not meaningful and likely reflects normal sample variation rather than a real difference in unit pricing.

Part 7. Analysis using Total Price (CHF)

Statistical Summary of Total Price by Property Status
is_hidden count median mean sd min max
Available 444 3000 3602.468 2499.159 30 22800
On Request 168 4900 5200.301 2749.578 1180 15000

INTERPRETATION: “On Request” properties shows a higher average and median total price than “Available” ones (about 4,030 CHF vs. 3,449 CHF, and 3,500 CHF vs. 2,767.5 CHF). This pattern suggests a right skewed distribution where hidden or un priced listings tend to fall into higher overall price ranges.

Part 7.1 T-Test

## 
##  Welch Two Sample t-test
## 
## data:  price by is_hidden
## t = -6.4815, df = 268.46, p-value = 0.0000000004329
## alternative hypothesis: true difference in means between group Available and group On Request is not equal to 0
## 95 percent confidence interval:
##  -2083.194 -1112.472
## sample estimates:
##  mean in group Available mean in group On Request 
##                 3602.468                 5200.301

OBSERVATION AND CONCLUSIONS: The t-test shows that “On Request” properties have a significantly higher average total price than “Available” ones. This points to a clear price gap between publicly listed properties and those with hidden or unlisted prices.
